svg.title: How a release reaches the Chrome Web Store
svg.desc: After every release, every day at 00:17 UTC and when started by hand with a tag, the workflow signs in to the Chrome Web Store and asks for the state of the item. A sign-in that Google turns away, a rejected release, a warning, a takedown or a review of more than 7 days fail the run, with the reason and the fix in its summary, and the bot-health sweep of the night keeps an issue open. While a review is pending, the run ends with a note, and a later day delivers the release. When the store has the release already, nothing happens. Otherwise a job without any secret takes the zip of the release and checks its provenance and its version; a release without a zip or a zip without a valid provenance fails the run. It keeps the zip as an artifact, and a job that reaches only Google compares its bytes, uploads it and submits it for review. When the store refuses the submission because the Developer Dashboard lacks something that the version needs, the run fails as well, and names what the release asks for beyond the version of the store. When a review began in the meantime, the run ends with the same note as for a pending review.
